outcome: Reduce the time required to understand and acknowledge the next incident requiring action.

evidence.claim: The fictional brief prioritizes identifying the highest-priority unresolved incident.
The fictional brief requires ownership and latest-update visibility.
Acknowledgement must work without opening a separate detail page.
The target includes 375 px and keyboard operation.
Production integrations and persistence are not specified and remain outside this prototype.

requirements.statement: The queue exposes unresolved incidents in priority order.
acceptance_criteria: The critical unresolved incident appears before lower-priority incidents.

requirements.statement: Every incident exposes its owner and latest meaningful update.
acceptance_criteria: Owner and latest update are visible without opening another route.

requirements.statement: A responder can acknowledge an incident from the queue.
acceptance_criteria: Activating Acknowledge changes the item state and announces the result.

requirements.statement: The critical journey works at 375 px and with keyboard input.
acceptance_criteria: At 375 px the page has no horizontal scrolling and all controls remain reachable in logical keyboard order.

decisions.choice: Sort unresolved critical incidents first and keep explicit priority labels.
decisions.alternative: Let users infer priority from color and arrival time.
decisions.tradeoff: The row carries more visible metadata but reduces ambiguity.
decisions.verification: Inspect the initial DOM order and visible labels.

decisions.choice: Keep owner and latest update in every queue row.
decisions.alternative: Show the information only in the detail panel.
decisions.tradeoff: Rows are taller in exchange for faster scanning.
decisions.verification: Inspect every incident row without selecting it.

decisions.choice: Use an inline button and polite live region for acknowledgement.
decisions.alternative: Require a modal confirmation for every acknowledgement.
decisions.tradeoff: The common action is faster; production policy may still require confirmation for higher-risk transitions.
decisions.verification: Activate by mouse and keyboard and inspect visible and announced state.

decisions.choice: Collapse the two-column workspace into one content-driven column below 760 px.
decisions.tradeoff: Detail moves below the queue, prioritizing the critical task over simultaneous context.
decisions.verification: Inspect at 375 px and test keyboard order.

verifications.evidence: Critical unresolved INC-248 appears first and carries a visible Critical label.
Each rendered incident includes owner and latest-update content.
The button updates its label, status chip, and aria-live region.
A 760 px media query creates one column; manual browser and assistive-technology checks remain required.
